title: Python & C++ for Verification
description: Hands-on coding prompts in Python and C/C++ used daily in SDK test harnesses and tools

questions.question: Write a Python function `parse_kv(line)` that parses "key=value" into a (key, value) tuple stripped of whitespace. Raise ValueError if "=" is missing.
questions.modelAnswer:
k, v = line.split("=", 1)
return k.strip(), v.strip()  # plus check for missing =
questions.explanation: Harnesses parse logs/config constantly — split once, strip, validate.

questions.question: Write a context manager class `chdir(path)` that temporarily changes the working directory and restores it afterward.
acceptedAnswers:
self.prev = os.getcwd()
        os.chdir(self.path)
        return self
    def __exit__(self, exc_type, exc, tb):
        os.chdir(self.prev)
questions.modelAnswer:
__enter__: save cwd, chdir to path
__exit__: chdir back to saved cwd
questions.explanation: Temporary chdir is common when tests rely on relative artifacts.

questions.question: In C++, what does RAII primarily help you manage?
options: Resource lifetime via object lifetime (ctors/dtors), reducing leaks and unlock bugs
Runtime reflection of all private members
questions.explanation: RAII ties resources (memory, locks, FDs) to scopes — critical in native SDK code.

questions.question: Write a C++ function signature and body for `int clamp(int x, int lo, int hi)` that returns x limited to [lo, hi]. Assume lo <= hi.
acceptedAnswers: int clamp(int x, int lo, int hi) { return std::max(lo, std::min(x, hi)); }
questions.explanation: Simple correctness under boundaries — interview warm-up for native code.

questions.question: Why might a Python verification harness shell out to a C++ stress binary instead of reimplementing it in Python?
questions.modelAnswer: To reuse production-like native paths, get higher performance/fidelity, and avoid reimplementing subtle protocol behavior in Python.
questions.explanation: Polyglot harnesses are normal: Python orchestrates, C/C++ hammers.

questions.question: Write a Python generator `tail_n(path, n)` that yields the last n lines of a text file efficiently enough for interview purposes (reading the file is OK).
questions.starterCode:
from collections import deque

def tail_n(path, n):
questions.modelAnswer:
with open(path) as f:
    yield from deque(f, maxlen=n)
questions.explanation: deque(maxlen=n) is the clean interview answer for tailing.

questions.question: Show how to prevent copying of a C++ class `DeviceHandle` (delete copy ctor and copy assignment).
acceptedAnswers:
DeviceHandle(const DeviceHandle&) = delete;
DeviceHandle& operator=(const DeviceHandle&) = delete;
questions.modelAnswer:
DeviceHandle(const DeviceHandle&) = delete;
DeviceHandle& operator=(const DeviceHandle&) = delete;
questions.explanation: Non-copyable handles prevent double-free / double-close bugs — RAII discipline.

questions.question: What is undefined behavior if you data-race a non-atomic int in C++?
options: The program may crash, corrupt data, or appear to work — UB means no guarantees
The compiler must insert a mutex automatically
Python will catch it with an exception
Linux converts it into a SIGKILL always
questions.explanation: Data races on non-atomics are UB in C++ — detectors and discipline matter.

questions.question: Write a Python function `classify_rc(rc)` that returns "pass" if rc==0, "skip" if rc==77, else "fail".
acceptedAnswers:
if rc == 0: return "pass"
    if rc == 77: return "skip"
    return "fail"
questions.modelAnswer:
if rc == 0: return "pass"
if rc == 77: return "skip"
return "fail"
questions.explanation: Exit-code taxonomies (including skip) show up in automations and CI.

questions.question: Name two differences between std::shared_ptr and std::unique_ptr that matter in SDK resource management.
questions.modelAnswer: unique_ptr: exclusive ownership, movable not copyable. shared_ptr: shared ownership with refcount, copies allowed.
questions.explanation: Ownership model choice prevents leaks and use-after-free in native stacks.

questions.question: Using pathlib, write code that creates directory reports/ uniquely if missing (parents OK) and writes "ok" into reports/status.txt.
questions.explanation: Idempotent artifact directories are CI hygiene.

questions.question: A C++ SDK API returns raw pointers the caller must free. What safer API design would you propose in a design review?
questions.modelAnswer: Return std::unique_ptr (or an RAII handle) so ownership and lifetime are explicit and exception-safe.
questions.explanation: Hands-on managers push API testability and safety in reviews.

followUpQuestions.question: RAII ties resource cleanup to…
followUpQuestions.explanation: RAII = resource lifetime follows object lifetime.

followUpQuestions.question: Create an empty set named s in Python.
followUpQuestions.explanation: {} is a dict; set() makes a set.

followUpQuestions.question: unique_ptr models what kind of ownership?
Why orchestrate tests in Python but stress in C++?
followUpQuestions.explanation: Python for glue; C++ for fidelity/performance.

levels.title: Basics
levels.tagline: Parsing, pathlib, pytest — with every line explained
levels.html:
def parse_kv(line):
    if "=" not in line:
        raise ValueError("missing =")
    k, v = line.split("=", 1)
    return k.strip(), v.strip()
  • split("=", 1) — split on the first = only (values may contain =).
  • strip() — remove surrounding whitespace.
  • ValueError — fail fast on bad input (better than silent wrong tuples).
python -c "from pathlib import Path; Path('reports').mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)"
Path(...).mkdir
Create directory.
parents=True
Create intermediate dirs if needed.
exist_ok=True
Do not error if it already exists (idempotent CI).

Virtual environments (do this before installing test deps)

python3 -m venv .venv
python3 -m venv
Create an isolated Python environment directory.
.venv
Folder name for the environment (common convention).
source .venv/bin/activate
source
Run the activate script in your current shell.
.venv/bin/activate
Puts this venv’s python/pip first on PATH.
pip install -r requirements.txt
pip install
Install packages into the active environment.
-r requirements.txt
Read package pins from the requirements file.
Why venv

CI and laptops diverge constantly. A venv + pinned requirements makes harness deps reproducible.

Running one test file verbosely

pytest -q -vv test_parse.py
pytest
Discover and run tests.
-q
Short summary.
-vv
Extra verbose assertion diffs / statuses.
test_parse.py
Only this file.

levels.title: Advanced
levels.html:
RAII: resource lifetime follows object lifetime — constructors acquire, destructors release.

#include <mutex>
#include <memory>

struct DeviceHandle {
  DeviceHandle();
  ~DeviceHandle();
  DeviceHandle(const DeviceHandle&) = delete;
  DeviceHandle& operator=(const DeviceHandle&) = delete;
};
  • = delete — forbid copying so you cannot double-close a handle.
  • std::unique_ptr<T> — exclusive ownership, movable.
  • std::shared_ptr<T> — shared ownership with refcount (use only with a clear shared lifetime).
Polyglot harnesses

Python orchestrates matrices and reporting; C++ stress binaries exercise production-like paths under sanitizers.

unique_ptr in practice

#include <memory>
std::unique_ptr<Device> open_device() {
  return std::make_unique<Device>(/* args */);
}
// ownership moves:
std::unique_ptr<Device> d = open_device();
  • make_unique — allocate and wrap safely (exception-safe).
  • Returning unique_ptr — transfers ownership to the caller clearly.
  • Copying unique_ptr — compile error (by design).

levels.title: Expert
levels.tagline: Sanitizer builds and API review instincts
levels.html:
g++ -fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-omit-frame-pointer -g -O1 main.cpp -o main
-fsanitize=address
ASan: catch heap-use-after-free, buffer overflows, etc.
-fsanitize=undefined
UBSan: catch many undefined behaviors.
-fno-omit-frame-pointer
Better stack traces.
-g -O1
Symbols + modest optimization for actionable reports.

In design reviews, push APIs that return unique_ptr/RAII handles — not raw “caller must free” pointers.

Hybrid answer

“Python owns the matrix and reporting; C++ owns the packet path under ASan/TSan builds.”

subprocess with a timeout (Python harness pattern)

import subprocess
subprocess.run(["./stress", "--seconds", "30"], check=True, timeout=90)
  • check=True — raise if exit code ≠ 0.
  • timeout=90 — kill hung stress jobs so CI agents don’t stick forever.
